Section 1512(b)(3)(A) is amended (1) by striking out “have a governing body for health planning, which is established in accordance with subparagraph (C),” and inserting in lieu thereof “appoint a governing body for health planning in accordance with subparagraph (C)”, (2) by striking out “which has exclusive” and inserting in lieu thereof “which shall have exclusive”, and (3) by striking out “not more than twenty-five members” and inserting in lieu thereof “not less than ten members and not more than thirty members”.

Section 15l2(b)(3)(B)(iv) is amended by striking out “(g), and (h)” and inserting in lieu thereof “and (g)”.

        (1) 
Paragraph (4) of section 1512(b) is amended to read as follows:


“(4) 
Liability.—

“(A) 
In general.—
Except as provided in subparagraph (B)—

“(i) 
a health systems agency shall not, by reason of the performance of any duty, function, or activity, required of, or authorized to be undertaken by, the agency, be liable for the payment of damages under any law of the United States or any State (or political subdivision thereof) if the member of the governing body of the agency or employee of the agency who acted on behalf of the agency in the performance of such duty, function, or activity acted within the scope of his duty, function, or activity as such a member or employee, exercised due care, and acted without malice toward any person affected by it; and


“(ii) 
no individual member of the governing body of a health systems agency or employee of a health systems agency shall, by reason of his performance on behalf of the agency of any duty, function, or activity required of, or authorized to be undertaken by, the agency, be liable for the payment of damages under any !aw of the United States or any State (or political subdivision of a State) if he believed he was acting within the scope of his duty, function, or activity as such a member or employee, and, with respect to such performance, acted without gross negligence or malice toward any person affected by it.



“(B) 
Exception.—
Subparagraph (A) does not apply with respect to civil actions for bodily injury to individuals or physical damages to property brought against a health systems agency or any member of the governing body of or employee of such an agency.”.




 
        (2) Section 1524 is amended by adding at the end thereof the following new subsection:


“(d) 
No individual who as a member or employee of a SHCC shall, by reason of his performance of any duty, function, or activity required of, or authorized to be undertaken by, the SHCC, be liable for payment of damages under any law of the United States or any State (or political subdivision of a State) if he believed he was acting within the scope of his duty, function, or activity as such a member or employee, and acted, with respect to that performance, without gross negligence or malice toward any person affected by it.”.

The first sentence of section 1512(b)(3)(A) is amended by striking out “to perform for the agency” and inserting in lieu thereof “to perform”.
 
        (2) 

            (A) 
Section 1512(b)(3)(B)(ii) is amended by inserting before the semicolon the following: “and in the case of a health systems agency which is a public regional planning body or unit of general local government, the planning body or unit of government shall be given, in accordance with sections 1513(b)(2) and 1513(b)(3), a reasonable opportunity to comment on the health systems plan and annual implementation plan proposed by the governing body and to propose additions to and other revisions in it”.
 
            (B) The amendment made by subparagraph (A) shall not apply with respect to a health systems agency for which a designation under section 1515 of the Public Health Service Act was in effect on January 1, 1979, and which is a unit of general local government.
  
        (3) Clauses (iii) and (iv) of section 1512(b)(3)(B) are each amended by striking out “approval” and inserting in lieu thereof “approval or disapproval”.
 
        (4) Section 1513(b)(2) is amended by adding at the end the following: “If the health systems agency is a public regional planning body or unit of general local government, the planning body or unit of government shall be given a reasonable opportunity to comment on the proposed HSP and to propose additions to and other revisions in it. Any such proposed additions or other revisions not included in the HSP established by the agency shall be appended to the HSP. If the goals contained in the HSP are not consistent with guidelines issued by the Secretary under section 1501, it shall provide the State health planning and development agency and the Secretary with a detailed statement of the reasons for the inconsistency between such goals and guidelines. When making such HSP available to a Statewide Health Coordinating Council under section 1524(c)(2)(A), the agency shall also report such statement to such Council.”
  
    (f) Section 1513(a) is amended by adding after the first sentence the following: “None of the funds authorized to be appropriated under this title may be used by a health systems agency directly to pay any individual to influence the issuance, amendment, or revocation of any Executive order or regulation by any Federal, State, or local chief executive officer or agency or to influence the passage, amendment or defeat of any legislation by the Congress or by any State or local legislative body. The preceding sentence does not apply with respect to compensation paid by a health systems agency to an employee of the agency unless the primary responsibility of the employee for the agency is to influence such governmental action.”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the "reasonable opportunity to comment" is a comment period, but the comment is on a health systems plan prepared by a health systems agency, which is itself a non-federal body (a nonprofit, regional planning body, or local government unit). No federal decision-maker is required to consult outsiders here; the exchange is between a local planning body and its own governing body for health planning. The remaining provisions concern liability immunity for agency members and a restriction on using funds for lobbying, neither of which grants outsiders a role in, or a right to sue over, a federal decision.
fable.s: the planning body or unit of government shall be given a reasonable opportunity to comment on the proposed HSP and to propose additions to and other revisions in it

qwen_block.w: This provision requires a public regional planning body or unit of general local government (outside entities) to be given a reasonable opportunity to comment on and propose revisions to the health systems plan. This constitutes participation by non-federal parties in the decision-making process regarding the plan. The requirement for comments and proposals from local governments fits the definition of participation.
qwen_block.s: the planning body or unit of government shall be given, in accordance with sections 1513(b)(2) and 1513(b)(3), a reasonable opportunity to comment on the health systems plan and annual implementation plan proposed by the governing body and to propose additions to and other revisions in it
qwen_block.b:
1. **Think briefly**: The section contains several amendments. Subsection (e)(2)(A) explicitly states that a "public regional planning body or unit of general local government shall be given... a reasonable opportunity to comment on the health systems plan... and to propose additions to and other revisions in it." This is a clear instance of requiring consultation/participation with outside entities (local governments) before a federal/state agency (the health systems agency) finalizes a plan. Subsection (e)(4) also requires giving a "reasonable opportunity to comment" to the planning body. While there are references to liability and lobbying restrictions, the comment requirement is a definitive "Yes" for participation. The tempting wrong reading might be that these are internal agency procedures, but the text specifies "public regional planning body or unit of general local government," which are outside the federal government.

opus.w: The comment opportunity runs between non-federal bodies: a local planning body or unit of government comments on a plan written by a non-federal health systems agency's governing body. No federal decision-maker is consulting outsiders, so this does not cross the federal boundary, just as in Example 9. The tempting 'Yes' reading treats any comment opportunity as participation, but the definition requires outside input into a federal decision, and the rest of the section is about governance, liability, and limits on lobbying.
opus.s: If the health systems agency is a public regional planning body or unit of general local government, the planning body or unit of government shall be given a reasonable opportunity to comment on the proposed HSP and to propose additions to and other revisions in it.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** Subsections (e)(2)(A) and (e)(4) give a "reasonable opportunity to comment" on health systems plans, which sounds like a comment period. That reading fails because no federal decision is involved. Health systems agencies under the Public Health Service Act's health planning title are regional nonprofits, public regional planning bodies, or local governments, not federal agencies. The plan is written by the agency's own governing body, and the comment right goes to a local planning body or unit of government. So both sides of the exchange are outside the federal government. This matches Example 9, where a state consulted its own officials on a plan it would submit; that was "No" because the consultation was not on a federal policy. The rest of the section covers governance, liability shields and limits on lobbying, with no federal consultation, hearing, rulemaking or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires that a local government entity (the planning body or unit of government) be given a reasonable opportunity to comment on a health systems plan. According to the definition, local governments are outside the federal government, and consultation or coordination with them constitutes participation. The tempting wrong reading is that because the commenter is a government entity, it is inside the government, but the definition explicitly excludes only federal entities from being 'outside'.

qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: It looks like participation because it refers to a "reasonable opportunity to comment" on a health systems plan.
Resolution: The entity receiving the opportunity to comment is the "planning body or unit of government," which is a local government entity. However, the definition states that local governments are OUTSIDE the federal government. Therefore, this is participation. Wait, let me re-read the definition carefully. "States, tribes, local governments... are OUTSIDE it." So consultation with a local government IS participation. The tempting wrong reading might be that because it's a government entity, it's inside. But the definition explicitly lists local governments as outside. So the label is Yes.

Let's double check.
Definition: "Participation is when the federal government may or must consult or coordinate with people outside of the government... These people might be state or local governments..."
Section: "...the planning body or unit of government shall be given, in accordance with sections 1513(b)(2) and 1513(b)(3), a reasonable opportunity to comment on the health systems plan..."
The "planning body or unit of government" is a local government. Local governments are outside the federal government. The federal agency (or the health systems agency acting under federal authority) must give them an opportunity to comment. This fits the definition of participation (consultation/coordination with outside entities).

Is there any reason to say No?
- Is the health systems agency a federal agency? The text says "health systems agency... which is a public regional planning body or unit of general local government". It seems these are local entities. The Secretary is involved in guidelines. The comment period is for the local planning body.
- The definition says: "consultation or coordination with states, tribes, local governments... before a federal action".
- Here, the health systems plan is being developed. The local government gets to comment. This is coordination with a local government.

Let's look for other parts.
"(4) Section 1513(b)(2) is amended by adding at the end the following: 'If the health systems agency is a public regional planning body or unit of general local government, the planning body or unit of government shall be given a reasonable opportunity to comment on the proposed HSP...'"

This is clearly participation with a local government.

Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that because the "planning body" is a government entity, it is "inside" the government. However, the definition explicitly states that local governments are OUTSIDE the federal government. Therefore, interaction with them counts as participation.
